audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers give Tryndamere four of seven stages and Trundle none (content win and full phases[].side are identical: Skill / Tryndamere / Tryndamere / Skill / Skill / Tryndamere / Tryndamere), while the same page rates the matchup 4/10 difficulty, calls it a "Favoured matchup" in report[14], and every single one of the seven whys describes Trundle winning that stage. Trundle wins 57.09% of 275 games. The `diff` field also says HARD against its own 4/10 rating.
audit.why: The chart card, the difficulty rating, the final rating line and all seven explanatory paragraphs disagree with each other on the same page. whys[0] through whys[5] are unambiguously Trundle-favourable — 'you feel it immediately', 'his E gap-close becomes an entry into your power island', 'he has no reliable disengage', 'he cannot out-sustain you', 'the clearest power spike of the matchup' — under stage labels that say Tryndamere wins.
audit.corrected: Trundle 1 through first item, Skill at two-plus items where the crit build lands, and diff FAV to match the 4/10 rating and report[14].

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3] locates Tryndamere's threat window "after his R expires", and `late` credits Kraken Slayer with a "percent-current-HP passive" that punches through armour.
audit.why: Both are backwards. Bloodlust increases his Attack Damage the more wounded he is, so his damage peaks exactly while Undying Rage is running and his health is near zero — the window is during the ultimate, not after it. And Kraken Slayer's proc is bonus true damage on a repeating attack count, not percent-current-health, so it is not an armour-penetration argument.
audit.corrected: His damage spike is inside Undying Rage, when Bloodlust's missing-health AD is at maximum.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mocking Shout does not appear anywhere on the page — not in spikes, wants, early, mid, late, whys, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull, dontsFull or report.
audit.why: It is the direct mirror of Trundle's own Chomp: it decreases surrounding champions' Attack Damage on a 14-second cooldown at 850 range, and — this is the part that decides retreats — Riot's text says enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere also have their Move Speed reduced. Walking away from a Tryndamere is slower than backing away facing him. That is a free, verifiable, kit-text fact that changes how every trade in this lane ends, and the page omits the ability entirely.
audit.corrected: Mocking Shout (14s, 850 range) saps your AD and slows you only if your back is turned — disengage facing him.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0] says Chomp's "AS slow means his next few autos hit slower too", and phases[2].why says to place Pillar of Ice "between you and Undying Rage to break his pattern".
audit.why: Chomp's slow is a movement slow; the ability saps Attack Damage, not attack speed, so nothing about it makes his autos land more slowly. And Undying Rage is a self-buff with no position to stand between — there is no line to block. Both sentences describe mechanics that do not exist and give a player a false read on what his cooldowns bought him.
audit.corrected: Chomp: damage, brief movement slow, AD sap. Pillar of Ice is spent behind him after Spinning Slash, not against his ultimate.

audit.whatIsWrong: Battle Fury is never mentioned, and the page treats his crit and his healing as if he gets both.
audit.why: Fury raises his critical strike chance and is consumed by Bloodlust to heal. A Tryndamere at full Fury is choosing: either he keeps the crit chance or he spends the bar on a heal. Watching that bar tells you which fight you are in, and it is the single tell that decides whether to commit before or after his heal.
audit.corrected: Full Fury is either a crit streak or a Bloodlust heal — he only spends it once.

audit.whatIsWrong: Undying Rage is named in nine fields and its cooldown appears in none of them; breakdown.cooldowns says "Track it before every engage" with no figure.
audit.why: Undying Rage is 120/100/80 seconds — the identical cooldown to Subjugate. That symmetry is the whole level-6 rule: the player who spends his ultimate second wins the exchange. Spinning Slash is 12/11/10/9/8s, Mocking Shout 14s, Bloodlust 12s, and Chomp is 3.5s flat, so between his spin cooldowns you get three bites.
audit.corrected: Undying Rage 120/100/80s = Subjugate 120/100/80s. Spinning Slash 12s at rank 1. Mocking Shout 14s.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] correctly prescribes Executioner's Calling on first back, but no field in either layer connects anti-heal to the moment it matters, and wants.you[2] tells you to sit through Undying Rage with no mention of Grievous Wounds.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags needs-antiheal for Bloodlust, and the timing is specific: Undying Rage guarantees he survives 5 seconds, so the fight is decided by whether Bloodlust can refill him the instant it ends. Grievous Wounds has to already be on him before the ultimate expires, not applied afterwards.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal must be applied before Undying Rage ends, not after.

audit.why: The packet's suspectName "Use Pillar of Ice" in wants.you[1] is a false positive — the name is correct. Separately, the kit file's derived flags give Spinning Slash no dash flag at all despite it being a dash, which is why the automated interaction pass never flagged Pillar of Ice against it; see notes.

edits.after: Chomp strips Tryndamere's AD — the one stat his entire damage model runs on — and Mocking Shout is his mirror of it, so bite first and the AD gap belongs to you.

edits.after: Frozen Domain plus Pillar of Ice is an E-trap: drop W, bait Spinning Slash — 12s at rank 1 — then slam the Pillar behind him and run him down before the spin is back.

edits.before: Subjugate into Frozen Domain at 6 is the cleanest all-in — Chomp drains his AD while you outlast his 5-second Undying Rage by standing on W and letting the ice heal carry you through it.
edits.after: Subjugate into Frozen Domain at 6 is the cleanest all-in — it takes 40% of his resists plus a fifth of his max health and heals you the same, which is what carries you through his 5s of Undying Rage.

edits.before: Tryndamere's Infinity Edge and Kraken Slayer crit spike can swing extended duels if he survives early — respect his burst window after his R expires before reengaging.
edits.after: Tryndamere's Infinity Edge and Kraken Slayer crit spike swings duels if he survives early — his AD peaks while Undying Rage runs, because Bloodlust scales off missing health.

edits.after: When Undying Rage fires, stand on Frozen Domain and keep biting — Grievous Wounds has to already be on him before the 5 seconds end, never applied afterwards

edits.before: Spin through your Pillar with E before it fully erupts, buying enough space to kite at the edge of Frozen Domain rather than standing inside it
edits.after: Open with Mocking Shout so Trundle's AD drops before his own does, then fight at the edge of Frozen Domain rather than standing inside it

edits.after: Let Battle Fury build to full crit, then spend it on Bloodlust only when the heal wins the trade — Fury cannot buy both at once

edits.before: Force all-ins when Subjugate is on cooldown so he cannot drain the armor he needs for the follow-through kill
edits.after: Force the all-in while Subjugate is down — 120s at rank 1, the same figure as his own Undying Rage ultimate

edits.before: At level 1 lead immediately with Q Chomp — you steal a percentage of Tryndamere's Attack Damage on contact, which is the exact resource his entire damage profile depends on. Every extended trade from this point on you are hitting harder while he hits softer, and King's Tribute heals you off the minion wave he is standing in. At level 2 drop Frozen Domain the moment he E-spins toward you: the movement speed spike lets you match his position before he can spin back out, and the additional AS means your next two Chomps land faster than he expects. At level 3 your Pillar becomes an E-trap — bait the spin-in with an auto, then slam the Pillar behind him so his only escape is directly into you on the ice zone.
edits.after: At level 1 lead with Chomp — you sap a percentage of Tryndamere's Attack Damage on contact, the exact resource his damage profile depends on, and it is back every 3.5 seconds. Every extended trade from here you hit harder while he hits softer, and King's Tribute heals you off the minions dying beside him. Expect Mocking Shout in return: it cuts your AD, it is down for 14 seconds, and it slows you only when your back is turned — so back out facing him. At level 2 drop Frozen Domain the moment he spins in; the move speed matches his position before Spinning Slash is back. At level 3 the Pillar becomes the trap — bait the spin with an auto, then wall the exit behind him.

edits.before: Level 6 is the most decisive window of the lane. Subjugate mid-trade does two things simultaneously: it drains Tryndamere's armor and MR onto you, and it fires as an extra burst of damage while Chomp continues shaving his AD. When he pops Undying Rage at 1 HP, do not panic-disengage — walk inside Frozen Domain and let the W healing sustain you through the 5-second window while auto-Chomping; by the time Undying Rage expires he has taken another two or three full Chomp stacks and you are still healthy. His only counter-play at this stage is to save R for your initiation and hope you misread its cooldown, so watch the buff bar and commit your all-in only after you see he has not yet activated it.
edits.after: Level 6 is the most decisive window of the lane. Subjugate does two things at once: it takes 40% of Tryndamere's armour and MR onto you, and it deals a fifth of his max health while healing you for the same, half of that over the next 4 seconds. Both ultimates sit on 120 seconds at rank 1, so whoever spends his second wins. When Undying Rage fires, do not panic-disengage — stand on Frozen Domain and keep Chomping through the 5 seconds; he leaves it as low as he entered unless Bloodlust refills him, which is why Executioner's Calling belongs on your first back. Watch his Fury bar as closely as his health bar: a full one is either a crit streak or a heal, never both.

edits.before: At two completed items Tryndamere's Infinity Edge and Kraken Slayer crit spike is real — he is no longer purely reliant on raw AD, and Kraken's percent-current-HP passive starts to punch through the armor you stacked from Subjugate. You still win the isolated 1v1 if you land the full Chomp-drain sequence, but the margin shrinks and one missed Pillar that lets him E freely through your Frozen Domain can flip the duel. Prioritize objectives and team fights where Subjugate on a tank or bruiser in their composition is worth more than the diminishing marginal returns on re-fighting a 3-item Tryndamere alone.
edits.after: At two completed items Tryndamere's Infinity Edge and Kraken Slayer crit spike is real — his damage stops living purely on base AD, so the slice Chomp saps is a smaller share of it than it was at level 1. You still win the isolated 1v1 if you land the full Chomp-drain sequence, but the margin shrinks and one missed Pillar of Ice — 21s at rank 1 — that lets him spin freely through your Frozen Domain can flip the duel. Prioritise objectives and team fights, where Subjugate on their tank is worth more than re-fighting a three-item Tryndamere alone.

edits.before: Your Chomp cooldown keeps ticking and King's Tribute heals off every minion wave death; he cannot out-sustain you in the extended trades this phase demands.
edits.after: Chomp is 3.5s flat and King's Tribute heals off every minion dying beside you; Bloodlust only answers that while he still has Fury banked and no Grievous Wounds on him.

edits.before: Iceborn Gauntlet's Frostfield aura and Chomp's synergy with the Spellblade proc extend your lane dominance into mid-game skirmishes and objective fights where he cannot freely E away.
edits.after: Iceborn Gauntlet's Spellblade frost field lands on the Chomp reset and holds him inside your zone, which is where Spinning Slash's 12-to-8-second cooldown decides whether he leaves at all.

edits.before: Bite his AD + anti-heal — your W out-duels his crits. Trundle wins by trading around Tryndamere's Undying Rage and cashing the pattern: bite his AD, anti-heal, out-duel him.
edits.after: Bite his AD + anti-heal — your W out-duels his crits. Undying Rage is 120s at rank 1, exactly as long as Subjugate, so the player who spends it second wins level 6.

edits.before: Tryndamere wins by landing Undying Rage, denying your pattern, and out-trading your engage windows.
edits.after: Tryndamere wins by surviving on Undying Rage, refilling with Bloodlust, and out-critting you later.

edits.before: - Tryndamere Undying Rage: matchup-defining — Unkillable 5s. Wait it out, then R-steal. Track it before every engage.
edits.after: - Undying Rage 120/100/80s: unkillable 5s, the same cooldown as your Subjugate. - Mocking Shout 14s slows only a turned back.

edits.after: Trade around Undying Rage's 120s: with it down, run the full pattern. With it up, chip on Frozen Domain and refuse the all-in.

edits.before: Pillar closes the kit — use it behind Tryndamere to deny disengage, or between you and Undying Rage to break his pattern.
edits.after: Pillar closes the kit — 21s at rank 1. Spend it behind him once Spinning Slash is gone and the ice zone becomes a box.

edits.before: Subjugate online — the 1v1 is yours into almost anyone the moment Tryndamere commits. R early in the all-in so the drained resists count for the whole fight.
edits.after: Subjugate online — 40% of his resists plus a fifth of his max health, healing you the same. Both ultimates are 120s at rank 1: make him spend first.

edits.after: Undying Rage: unkillable 5s, 120/100/80s — the same cooldown as Subjugate. Mocking Shout slows only a turned back.

notes: Kit-file flag gap worth fixing upstream: Spinning Slash carries no dash flag in champ-data/_kits/tryndamere.json even though it is a dash, which is why _missing-interactions.json never raised Pillar of Ice against it for this matchup the way it did for Zaahen. Because of that I did not add any new claim that Pillar of Ice stops the spin — the page already asserts it in wants.you[1] and denies it in wants.foe[0], and I removed the contradiction by rewriting wants.foe[0] around Mocking Shout instead of adjudicating it. See questionsForUser. `diff` said HARD while diffRating said 4/10 and report[14] said 'Favoured matchup'; I set diff to FAV, which is the value used by 7 other entries in this file.
